newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS - Russian market to boom on new certainty.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Russian market to boom on new certainty.

text.p: The Russian equities market is set to grow exponentially thanks to a new securities market policy which puts an end to regulatory uncertainty, Russian Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Friday.

Chubais said commercial banks would play a key role in stock market growth, and he backed German-style ties between banks and industry which are already apparent in powerful Russian financial-industrial groups.

"We are talking about hundreds of billions of dollars of potential growth of the volume of the Russian equities market," Chubais told a news conference. "The decisions taken yesterday make it possible to talk about that with certainty."
Chubais said Russian stock market capitalisation could grow by dozens of times as new issuers came to market.

Russian market capitalisation has nearly doubled since the beginning of the year to $90 billion currently, chiefly on sharp price appreciation of a handful of leading shares. Chubais gave no time frame for his forecast.
He said the government had abandoned the principle of regulating the government securities and equities markets separately, removing major elements of uncertainty.

"The Central Bank and the securities commission will both regulate the market -- we will not divide the spheres of regulation," Chubais said. "There will be one market, one depository, one registrar."

Chubais's decision, the end of a long-running turf war for control of commercial bank activity on the equities market, divides regulatory responsibility between the Central Bank and the Federal Commission for the Securities Market.

An agreement signed on Thursday by representatives of the commission -- which wants full control of licensing and envisions a U.S.-style securities market -- the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank, allows the Central Bank to license commercial banks and credit organisations as of January 1, 1998.
Most other operators will be licensed to work on the securities markets by the commission.
Current securities market licences for banks running until October will be extended to January.
Chubais said commercial banks would be an important equities market supporter as in Germany, where banks have long-term relationships with companies in which they hold shares.

In the U.S.-British model stock markets are economic centres driven by active share trading by mutual fund and other large investors. German share markets are much smaller as many shares are held long-term by commercial banks.
About 60 registered financial-industrial groups linking major industries and banks already control a large part of the Russian economy.

"The Russian system has characteristics copying those of the German system, I mean the real interest and the real positions of the commercial banks not only in credit activity but in acquiring shares," Chubais said.
He said the Russian market, with a trading system similar to the U.S. over-the-counter NASDAQ system, would develop uniquely -- and had far greater potential for growth.
"The Russian securities market will be the best securities market in the world, and neither the German or the Americans have shown the potential for growth that we have already this year," he said.
